newsitem.title: HONG KONG: ITC gets go-ahead light on bonds issue.
newsitem.headline: ITC gets go-ahead light on bonds issue.

text.p: Civil engineering group International Tak Cheung Holdings Ltd (ITC) said on Thursday its shareholders had approved the company's plan to issue US$15 million in 6.875 percent convertible guaranteed bonds due 1999.
The company said an option would be granted to require the issuer to issue an additional US$2.0 million worth of bonds.
Net proceeds will be for general working capital, it said.
The bond issue has been arranged by CEF Capital Ltd and Creditanstalt Asia Ltd.
The bonds are primarily offered to institutional and professional investors in Europe and in Asia but will not be offered to investors in the United States, it said.
The bonds can be converted into the company's shares at a conversion price of HK$1.404 per share subject to adjustment.
Assuming full conversion of US$17 million in bonds, some 93.6 million new shares, or 25.3 percent of enlarged share capital, will be issued, it said.
The bonds which will be listed in Luxembourg, will be redeemed on October 4, 1999, at 108.837 percent of their aggregate princiapl amount together with accured interest.
ITC shares were up two cents to HK$1.30 in afternoon trade.
